# R5 Digest — Babel / Shemites; Abraham Cycle Part I (Gen 11–15)
**Coverage:** Full cache slice read sequentially (slice lines 1–1346 = raw 6045–7390). Sections complete: I. Shinarites and Shemites (11:1–32); II. Abraham Cycle Part I open — A. Emergence of Abram (12:1–20); B. Separation of Lot (13:1–18); C. Militant Abram and the kings (14:1–24); D. Covenant with Abram (15:1–21). Did not stop short. No internal ebook duplication flagged. Ishmael appears only prospectively (age/crisis chronology notes at 16:16); no dedicated Ishmael narrative in range.

**Source:** Victor P. Hamilton, *The Book of Genesis, Chapters 1–17* (NICOT), commentary on Gen 11:1–15:21 (translations + exposition + NT Appropriation blocks).

## Claims

### C-V1R5-01 | Gen 1–11 brackets narratives with genealogies; Babel framed by Shemite lists
- **Claim (attributed Hamilton):** Opening Genesis brackets narrative blocks by genealogical citations thrice: (1) 5:32 / 6:1–8 / 6:9–10; (2) 6:9–10 / Flood / 9:18–19; (3) 10:21–31 Shemites / 11:1–9 Babel / 11:10–32 Shemites — literary artistry also explaining order of chs. 10 and 11.
- **Quote:** "It is a distinguishing feature of these opening chapters of Genesis to bracket narrative blocks by genealogical citations… (This literary artistry provides another reason for the order of chs. 10 and 11.)"
- **Locus:** slice ~ll. 50–92; §I after 11:1–9 translation
- **Targets:** [[genesis]], [[toledot]], [[hamilton-genesis-1-17-nicot]], [[victor-hamilton]]

### C-V1R5-02 | One language (11) vs multiple languages (10): dischronologization or lingua franca
- **Claim (attributed Hamilton):** Apparent contradiction of 11:1 (one language/speech) with thrice-stated multiple languages in ch. 10 (vv. 5, 20, 31) may be deliberate dischronologization, or Gen 10 local *lešōnōṯ* plus ch. 11 one international *šāpâ* (lingua franca — Sumerian, Babylonian, Aramaic, Greek; modern English analogy).
- **Quote:** "in addition to the local languages (lešōnōṯ) of each nation (ch. 10), there existed “one language” (šāpâ’eḥāṯ, ch. 11) which made communication possible throughout the world"
- **Locus:** slice ~ll. 94–98
- **Targets:** [[genesis]], [[hamilton-genesis-1-17-nicot]], [[victor-hamilton]]

### C-V1R5-03 | Babel structure: human speech/deed vs divine speech/deed; irony of “peak in heavens”
- **Claim (attributed Hamilton):** Human deeds (vv. 3–4) contrast divine deeds (vv. 6–9); both use *hāḇâ* + cohortative; tower *migdāl* (related to *gāḏôl*) as fortified pride-symbol; “peak in the heavens” is figurative monumental language (Deut 1:28; 9:1; Jer 51:53); irony that God must come down to inspect (v. 5); Kikawada’s three-episode structure with v. 5 as thin midpoint.
- **Quote:** "even though they build the tower, it is so far from the heavens that God must come down to see it."
- **Locus:** slice ~ll. 108–125
- **Targets:** [[genesis]], [[hamilton-genesis-1-17-nicot]], [[victor-hamilton]]

### C-V1R5-04 | Babel sin: pride/humanism and settled security; city not tower alone halted
- **Claim (attributed Hamilton):** God takes the scheme seriously (not a joke); *bāṣar*/*zāmam* parallel Job 42:2 inverted — nothing would restrain human purpose if project continues; confuses language rather than topples tower (towers replaceable); *nāḇelâ*/*leḇēnîm* sound-chiasmus; sin is pride and pretentious humanism plus preference for homogeneous centralization; conclusion focuses on stopping the *city*, not the tower per se.
- **Quote:** "This indicates that it was the building of the city, and not the tower per se, that provoked the divine displeasure."
- **Locus:** slice ~ll. 126–138
- **Targets:** [[genesis]], [[hamilton-genesis-1-17-nicot]], [[victor-hamilton]]

### C-V1R5-05 | Babel name: popular etymology *bālal* / *babel* vs Akkadian “gate of god”
- **Claim (attributed Hamilton):** Builders wanted a *šēm* and got a name of shame; narrator connects *bālal* “confuse” with *babel* as popular nonliteral etymology (cannot derive place-name from *bālal*); oldest extrabiblical name ká-dingir-ki / *bab-ili(m)* “gate of god(s)” differs from Gen 11:9.
- **Quote:** "there is a clear difference between the explanation of Babylon in cuneiform languages and Gen. 11:9, which connects the name with the verb bālal, “to confuse.”"
- **Locus:** slice ~ll. 140–144
- **Targets:** [[genesis]], [[genesis-ancient-near-east]], [[hamilton-genesis-1-17-nicot]], [[victor-hamilton]]

### C-V1R5-06 | Babel not monogenesis-of-language etiology; Hamite/Shinar/Nimrod link
- **Claim (attributed Hamilton):** Unlikely Gen 11:1–9 explains origin of languages (diversification is slow; better as dissolution of Babylonian lingua franca); scenario in Shinar linked to Nimrod (10:9–10), grandson of Ham — Ham involved directly/indirectly in both post-Flood sin scenes (9:20ff.; 11:1–9).
- **Quote:** "If, however, the narrative refers to the dissolution of a Babylonian lingua franca… the need to see Gen.11:1—9 as a highly imaginative explanation of language diffusion becomes unnecessary."
- **Locus:** slice ~ll. 146–154
- **Targets:** [[genesis]], [[genesis-ancient-near-east]], [[hamilton-genesis-1-17-nicot]], [[victor-hamilton]]

### C-V1R5-07 | Shem genealogy 11:10–26: linear-to-segmented; novel names; chronological positions
- **Claim (attributed Hamilton):** 11:10ff. close to 10:21–31 but firstborn-only and deeper (five → ten generations); novel names Reu, Serug, Nahor, Terah, Abram; Serug/Nahor/Terah have Mari-area place counterparts (Sarug, Nahur, Turahi); structure like ch. 5 linear ending segmented; Enoch/Eber/Abram at positions divisible by seven or ten (Abram tenth from Shem, twentieth from Adam; LXX Kenan insertion → twenty-first); MT/LXX/SP disagree on ages after Shem.
- **Quote:** "Abram is tenth from Shem, and twentieth from the creation of Adam."
- **Locus:** slice ~ll. 258–278
- **Targets:** [[genesis]], [[toledot]], [[abraham]], [[genesis-ancient-near-east]], [[hamilton-genesis-1-17-nicot]], [[victor-hamilton]]

### C-V1R5-08 | Terah unit 11:27–32: migration parallel to Babel; moon-cult milieu
- **Claim (attributed Hamilton):** Terah fathers Abram, Nahor, Haran; Lot; Sarai barren; Terah leaves Ur of the Chaldeans with Abram, Sarai, Lot for Canaan, settles Haran; structural parallel of groups moving east→west and “settling” (*yāšaḇ*): Babel ends in frustration/dispersal; Terahite migration is incipient blessing/election of Abram; names (Terah/yārēaḥ; Sarai/sarratu–Ningal; Milcah/Malkatu; Laban/leḇānâ) and cult centers Ur and Haran suggest moon-worship milieu.
- **Quote:** "it is probable that the theological milieu in which Abram lived for a good bit of his life was one in which the cult focused its adoration on moon worship."
- **Locus:** slice ~ll. 280–284
- **Targets:** [[abraham]], [[genesis]], [[genesis-ancient-near-east]], [[hamilton-genesis-1-17-nicot]], [[victor-hamilton]]

### C-V1R5-09 | Ur of the Chaldeans: northern identification preferred over Sumerian Ur
- **Claim (attributed Hamilton):** Debate: Woolley’s southern Sumerian Ur vs northern Upper Mesopotamia (Urfa/Edessa; Ura; “Ur in Haran”); Hamilton judges balance favors northern Ur — long Fertile-Crescent detour, absence of “Ur of the Chaldeans” in cuneiform, late Chaldean arrival, Gen 24:4,7 birthplace in Aram-Naharaim, LXX *chṓra* “land,” northern place-name relatives (Til Turaḫi, Nahuru, Sarugi); southern counterarguments not decisive.
- **Quote:** "In our opinion, however, none of these arguments is decisive, and the balance of evidence favors a northern Ur."
- **Locus:** slice ~ll. 286–294
- **Targets:** [[abraham]], [[genesis-ancient-near-east]], [[hamilton-genesis-1-17-nicot]], [[victor-hamilton]]

### C-V1R5-10 | NT Appropriation: Babel with Luke 14:28–30 and Magnificat scatter
- **Claim (attributed Hamilton):** Only NT unfinished-tower abandonment parallel is Luke 14:28–30 (roles of mockers reversed vs Babel); Mary’s “scattered the proud” (Luke 1:51) fits Babel; LXX *diaskorpízō* for Hiphil *pûṣ* elsewhere though Gen 11 uses *diaspeírō*.
- **Quote:** "In the Genesis event the erection of the tower starts out as a project, part of whose aim is to mock God. But the roles are reversed"
- **Locus:** slice ~ll. 300–314; NT Appropriation after ch. 11

### C-V1R5-11 | NT Appropriation: Terah chronology and Acts 7:4
- **Claim (attributed Hamilton):** MT: Terah 70 at Abram’s birth (or first begetting), dies 205; Abram leaves Haran at 75 — so sixty-five years before father’s death if 11:26 means Abram born at 70; Acts 7:4 says left after Terah’s death. Options: SP/Philo 145; Palestinian text plurality; or 11:26 = began begetting at 70, Abram born near Terah 130 (parallel Noah’s sons not age-ordered; Ham youngest 9:24). Bruce rejects late birth as “improbable expedient,” prefers Greek agreeing with Samaritan 145.
- **Quote:** "The basic tenet of this approach is that 11:26 does not say that Terah was seventy years old when he fathered Abram. Rather, it says that Terah was seventy years old when he began to beget."
- **Locus:** slice ~ll. 318–336
- **Targets:** [[abraham]], [[genesis]], [[hamilton-genesis-1-17-nicot]], [[victor-hamilton]]

### C-V1R5-12 | Call structure 12:1–9: imperative + triple object; covenant not yet; show→give
- **Claim (attributed Hamilton):** First and last words to Abram (12:1; 22:1) begin with imperative + triple object (less→more intimate); terminal point not explicit (“land which I will show you” // mountain “of which I shall tell you”); covenant not yet (ch. 15); command and promises antedate covenant; faith already operates; promise to *give* land (v. 7) follows promise to *show* (v. 1) only when Abram moves; Haran not domicile (like ark for Noah).
- **Quote:** "The covenant is not mentioned at this point; that will come in ch. 15. Both the command of God (v. 1) and the promises of God (vv. 2—3) antedate the implementation of the covenant."
- **Locus:** slice ~ll. 396–398
- **Targets:** [[abraham]], [[covenant]], [[promised-land]], [[genesis]], [[hamilton-genesis-1-17-nicot]], [[victor-hamilton]]

### C-V1R5-13 | Seven-clause blessing 12:2–3; *gôy* nationhood; name vs Babel; royal language
- **Claim (attributed Hamilton):** Exclusive of command, blessing has seven clauses (heptad penchant); first: make great *gôy* (not *ʿam*) — nationhood with government/territory among the *gôyîm*; second: bless you (against Sarai’s barrenness 11:30); third: great name — deliberate contrast to Babel self-naming; gift not achievement; royal idiom shared with David (2 Sam 7:9; Ps 72:17); kings from Abram/Sarah (17:6, 16); “prince” *nāśîʾ* (23:6) = LXX *basileús*; does not force post-monarchy composition.
- **Quote:** "This is doubtless another deliberate contrast with the Tower of Babel incident… If his name is ever to become great it will not be because of any self-initiated effort. The great name will be a gift, not an achievement."
- **Locus:** slice ~ll. 402–410
- **Targets:** [[abraham]], [[genesis]], [[promised-land]], [[hamilton-genesis-1-17-nicot]], [[victor-hamilton]]

### C-V1R5-14 | “Be a blessing” as middle imperative; Niphal *niḇreḵû* passive, not reflexive
- **Claim (attributed Hamilton):** Imperative “and be a blessing” depends on prior “go” (cause→effect); middle of seven phrases — Abram receptacle and transmitter; climactic perfect: by you all earth’s clans blessed (Gen 10 peoples). Niphal (12:3; 18:18; 28:14) vs Hithpael (22:18; 26:4): moderns often “bless themselves”; Speiser: theologically consequential; Albrektson/Weinfeld favor reflexive against Heilsgeschichte plan; Hamilton retains passive — Hithpaels may be passive; “bless oneself” stretched; illustrations: Laban (30:27), Potiphar (39:5), Egypt via Joseph.
- **Quote:** "If the verb in question has passive force, then 12:3 clearly articulates the final goal in a divine plan for universal salvation, and Abram is the divinely chosen instrument in the implementation of that plan."
- **Locus:** slice ~ll. 412–436
- **Targets:** [[abraham]], [[covenant]], [[genesis]], [[hamilton-genesis-1-17-nicot]], [[victor-hamilton]]

### C-V1R5-15 | Abram’s silent obedience; Lot “presumed heir”; Shechem theophany and land to seed
- **Claim (attributed Hamilton):** Source critics assign chronological 4b–5 to P and rest to J; Hamilton: double Lot notation may foreshadow Lot dispute, not sources. Lot as “teasing motif of the presumed heir.” Shechem / terebinth of Moreh; theophany (vs prior audition) augments dramatic force; land to *descendants* eliminates Lot as heir; promise not for Abram’s lifetime yet; altar not tower/city; tents dismantled, altars left; invoke name = technical worship term in Pentateuch; Shechem–Bethel–Negeb path parallels Jacob and conquest route.
- **Quote:** "This promise clearly eliminates Lot as the presumptive heir. The heir will be Abram’s own seed."

### C-V1R5-16 | Egypt wife-sister (12:10–20): famine sojourn; half-truth; actual adultery
- **Claim (attributed Hamilton):** Famine drives sojourn to Egypt (Lot unmentioned — peripheral); Egyptian parallels: Beni Hasan Asiatics painting; Sinuhe (inverse itinerary); Merneptah Bedouin text. Sister ruse half-truth (20:12); Speiser’s Nuzi sister-adoption rejected (sequence artificial; not elite-only; etc.); Uriah–Bathsheba logic: siblings tolerable, spouses not. Pharaoh takes Sarai into palace — actual adultery (v. 19 “I took her for my wife”), not potential as 20:3–4. Abram prospers by animals/servants (camels anachronism debate: Albright vs Alalakh evidence).
- **Quote:** "This is doubtless a case of actual adultery between Pharaoh and Sarai, rather that potential adultery such as we find in 20:3—4."

- **Claim (attributed Hamilton):** Parallel abductions: Sarai *lāqaḥ* (12:15) // Lot *lāqaḥ* (14); both outside promised land. ### C-V1R5-26 | Melchizedek: king-priest of Salem; El Elyon creator; bread and wine; tithe direction
- **Claim (attributed Hamilton):** Meeting at King’s Valley (Shaveh) near Jerusalem environs prepares Melchizedek of Salem (= Jerusalem via Ps 76:3; uru-salim Sumerian “city”; 1QapGen 22:13). Name descriptive “my king is just/legitimate” (not necessarily theophoric). Priest of *ʾēl ʿelyôn* — v. 22 identifies with Yahweh; *qōnēh* “creator” (not only “possessor”) supported by Karatepe *ʾl qn ʾrṣ*, Ugaritic, Kilamuwa. Blessing actualizes “those who bless you I will bless”; *miggēn* “delivered” // *māgēn* 15:1 links chapters. Tithe: traditional subject Abram→Melchizedek (Heb 7:6; 1QapGen); not tax but postbellum booty distribution (Num 31:17; 1 Sam 30).

### C-V1R5-30 | Gen 15:6: first *heʾĕmîn*; Hiphil nuances; *ḥāšaḇ*…*ṣeḏāqâ* credit formula
- **Claim (attributed Hamilton):** First biblical Hiphil *ʾaman* “believe” (again only Gen 42:20; 45:26); action of faith preceded vocabulary (12:1ff.). *be* vs *le* prepositions; Hiphil not causative “make firm”; rejects Speiser declarative-estimative (needs direct object); delocutive “declared Amen” possible; traditional internal-transitive: “became steadfast in Yahweh.” Ambiguity of subject of *wayyaḥšeḇehā* (God or Abram?) — normal syntax could continue Abram; wider context and Paul (Rom 4:3) favor God credits Abram. Idiom *ḥāšaḇ* + acc. + *le*: reckon to account (2 Sam 19:20; Ps 32:2; Lev 7:18; 17:4; Num 18:27; Prov 27:14); von Rad’s cultic-declaratory origin via Leviticus; Hamilton via Seybold: Yahweh’s conscious judgment reckoning faith as deciding factor in relationship.
- **Quote:** "he credited it to him as righteousness… ḥāšaḇ “defines Yahweh’s momentary reaction theologically as an act of conscious judgment.”"
- **Locus:** slice ~ll. 1120–1142
- **Targets:** [[abraham]], [[covenant]], [[genesis]], [[hamilton-genesis-1-17-nicot]], [[victor-hamilton]]

### C-V1R5-31 | Covenant ceremony 15:7–17: animal pieces; ANE parallels; unilateral theophany not self-curse
- **Claim (attributed Hamilton):** Second vision unit: “I am Yahweh who brought you from Ur…” // Exod 20:2 pattern; Abram’s *bammâ* “how know?” not castigated. Three three-year animals halved + unsplit birds; only clear OT parallel Jer 34:18–19 (vassal passes between). ANE: Alalakh Abban–Yarimlim sheep-oath; Mari *ḫayaram qaṭālum*; Hittite purification halves (not treaty); Sefire and Esarhaddon closer to Jeremiah. Hamilton: Gen 15 not primarily Drohritus/self-curse on God; slaughter ratifies; only deity-symbol (smoking pot, flaming torch) passes between → unilateral; *ʿāḇar* theophanic (// Exod 33–34; Josh 3–4 sixfold pattern). Birds of prey driven off = Abram protecting seed (// ch. 14). Chronology: day 2 of vision (v. 5 night stars; v. 11 daytime raptors). Deep sleep and *ʾêmâ* terror from presence, not guilt.
- **Quote:** "That only something representing deity passes between the rows of flesh shows that this covenant is unilateral… It is not necessary to read into Gen. 15:17 any sanctions or self-curse to which Yahweh exposes himself."
- **Locus:** slice ~ll. 1212–1298
- **Targets:** [[covenant]], [[abraham]], [[promised-land]], [[genesis-ancient-near-east]], [[hamilton-genesis-1-17-nicot]], [[victor-hamilton]]

### C-V1R5-32 | 400 years exile prophecy; Amorite iniquity; *berîṯ* as imposed obligation/gift; land boundaries
- **Claim (attributed Hamilton):** Descendants strangers, enslaved, oppressed 400 years (Acts 7:6) ≈ round figure vs Exod 12:40–41 430 (Gal 3:17) more precise retrospect; land of sojourn unnamed (Abram may assume Egypt); God will judge oppressing nation; depart with *reḵuš* (// 12; 14:16, 21); Abram dies peaceful ripe old age; fourth *dôr* = lifetime (Albright); entry when Amorite iniquity complete — moral condition of times; Joshua as justice not aggression. V. 18 only “covenant” word in ch.: *berîṯ* ~ Akk. *birītu* “clasp, fetter” — obligation imposed; here only on Yahweh (Westermann: “solemn assurance”); parallel Davidic covenant unconditionality/oath/gift (land-for-all vs dynasty-for-one). Bounds: river of Egypt = Wadi el-Arish not Nile → Euphrates; ten nations; only Davidic apogee approximates, one generation.
- **Quote:** "Nothing, however, in this chapter is imposed on Abram… The only imposition or obligation that Yahweh lays upon anybody is upon himself"
- **Locus:** slice ~ll. 1248–1306
- **Targets:** [[covenant]], [[promised-land]], [[abraham]], [[genesis]], [[hamilton-genesis-1-17-nicot]], [[victor-hamilton]]

### C-V1R5-33 | NT Appropriation: 15:6 in Rom 4 / Gal 3 and Jas 2:20–24
- **Claim (attributed Hamilton):** Rom 4 test-cases 3:21–31 righteousness-by-faith; Paul quotes LXX passive; “reckoned” shows grace not wages; David (Ps 32) balances pre-/post-Sinai. James not at loggerheads: chiastic faith–works focus; “justified by works” demonstrative (“shown to be just”); sequence/evidence not meritorious path; Abraham + Rahab extremes; circumvents legalism and fideism.
- **Quote:** "When James says that Abraham was “justified by works” (v. 21), he is surely using the verb with demonstrative force… “Abraham was shown to be just by works.”"
- **Locus:** slice ~ll. 1310–1342
- **Targets:** [[abraham]], [[covenant]], [[hamilton-genesis-1-17-nicot]], [[victor-hamilton]]

### C-V1R5-34 | Hermeneutical frame of this slice (Hamilton)
- **Claim (attributed Hamilton / method):** Hamilton combines literary structure (brackets, chiasmus, heptads, narrative irony), philology (Hebrew syntax, etymologies, text-critical MT/LXX/SP), ANE comparative parallels (without forcing Speiser/Nuzi maximalism where evidence fails), resistance to source-critical default assignments (P chronology, independent Gen 14), theological reading of promise–covenant development (command/promise before *berîṯ*; unilateral gift), and explicit NT appropriation sections for each major unit.
